raw_signal: רשמתי מהלך והלוח לא זז. הכלי עדיין במקום שלו, והריבוע השני נראה בדיוק כמו לפני שלחצתי.
observations: Selecting the b5 pawn draws a gold ring on b5 and a gold ring with a centre dot on b4, its one legal destination.
Clicking b4 to choose the move leaves both marks exactly as they were. The piece stays on b5 and no piece appears on b4.
The only visible change is in a 291px side column: step 1 changes from 'בחרו מהלך על הלוח' to 'b5b4', and the commit button relabels to the next missing item.
The board occupies 616x616 at 1440x900 and 405x405 on a handset; the side column is 291px wide and, on a handset, below the board.
A live region says 'המהלך שהצעתם: b5 אל b4' and 'b5b4 נבחר. אפשר עדיין לשנות עד לרישום.'; neither is where the eye was.
Clicking an empty square, e8, gives it the same gold selection ring as a square holding a piece, with zero destinations shown.

candidate_mechanisms.name: The board deliberately does not execute the move, because a decision is a claim and not a played move
candidate_mechanisms.explains: Why the piece stays put after commit-time selection and why the move only appears as an arrow after the reveal.
candidate_mechanisms.does_not_explain: Why intent and choice share one visual vocabulary, when the design has a second one available and uses it later.
candidate_mechanisms.discriminator: Ask the owner directly: is 'chosen but not yet recorded' meant to be distinguishable on the board, or only in the panel?

candidate_mechanisms.name: The destination marker is a hover/selection affordance reused as the chosen-move marker
candidate_mechanisms.explains: Why the dot looks the same before and after the choice.
candidate_mechanisms.does_not_explain: The empty-square ring, which is a third state using the same mark.
candidate_mechanisms.discriminator: Select a piece with several legal destinations and choose one. If the unchosen destinations disappear, the marker is doing double duty and the states are separable; if they stay, they are not.

design_distinction: Three states share one mark: 'I am pointing at this square', 'I could go here', and 'this is my decision'. The instrument depends on the third being a deliberate act, so it is the one that most needs its own appearance.
rejected_explanations: Slow render: the panel updates within 400ms; the board is not lagging, it is unchanged by design.
must_not_change: That the move is not played on the board before commit. That is the protocol, not a bug, and removing it would let the position advance before the decision is recorded.
perceptual_success_criterion: A person who has chosen a move can point at the board, not at the panel, and say which move they chose.
next_step: Run the second discriminator, it costs one session: choose among several legal destinations and see whether the rejected ones clear. Then put the owner question, because the answer decides whether this is a defect at all.
